wording.value: I've been learning Polish for a year.
Przepraszam, nie mówię dobrze po polsku.
Sorry, I don't speak Polish well.
I'm not from here, I'm a tourist.
How do you spell your surname?
Excuse me, I have a question.
Przepraszam, czy może mi pan pomóc?
Excuse me, can you help me?
To a woman: 'Czy może mi pani...'
Warm way to end a chat.
Masculine phrase. 'Jaki masz numer?' = what's your number?
Masculine noun. 'Pod jakim adresem?' = at what address?
I've been married for five years. A woman: Jestem mężatką.
A man is 'żonaty', a woman is 'mężatka'.
W rubryce stan cywilny wpisałem: kawaler.
In the marital-status box I wrote: kawaler (single). A woman: panna.

These are the official marital-status words you tick on forms, and they sound old-fashioned as everyday labels. In conversation Poles say 'jestem singlem' / 'jestem singielką', or simply 'nie jestem w związku'.
He is a doctor at the hospital.
'iść do lekarza' = to go to the doctor.
My brother is a bus driver.
Masculine, but ends in -a. Same form for a woman.
Nie wiem, co wybrać. Co pan poleca?
I don't know what to pick. What do you recommend?
To have here or take away?
Said before eating. The usual reply is 'Dziękuję'. If the other person is also eating, you can add 'nawzajem' (you too).
Excuse me, is there wi-fi here?
What staff often ask you. You'll hear both 'Coś jeszcze?' and 'Jeszcze coś?'.
Colours and the clothes you wear every day
What colour do you like most?
Adjective. Also means 'inexperienced', like in English.
Adjective. 'szary' also means dull or drab.
I need to buy new clothes.
Neuter noun. Often used in plural: 'ubrania'.
I'm wearing a T-shirt and jeans.
Feminine noun. 'koszula' is a formal shirt.
I bought a new dress for the wedding. A man: kupiłem.
In winter I always wear a hat.
Feminine noun. Essential for a Polish winter.
noszę, nosisz. For what you wear regularly.
Informal. A shop assistant will ask: 'Jaki rozmiar pan/pani nosi?'
'To mi pasuje' = that suits me / works for me.
Days of the week and talking about time
On Tuesday I have a Polish lesson.
On Wednesday I go to the gym.
'w środę' = on Wednesday. Literally 'the middle' of the week.
On Thursday I have a meeting.
'w czwartek' = on Thursday. From 'cztery' (four) - the fourth day.
W piątek wieczorem spotykam się ze znajomymi.
On Friday evening I meet up with friends.
On Sunday the shops are closed.
'w niedzielę' = on Sunday. Most shops in Poland are closed on Sundays.
What are you doing at the weekend?
Both forms are common and interchangeable.
Yesterday I was at the cinema.
'przedwczoraj' = the day before yesterday. A woman says: byłam.
In the morning I drink coffee.
In the afternoon I have time.
In the evening I watch a series.
At what time do we start?
I get up at seven in the morning.
Times use ordinal numbers: o siódmej, o ósmej, o dziewiątej.
Excuse me, what time is it?
The everyday way to ask for the time.
Mam wolny dzień w tym tygodniu.
I have a day off this week.
'nigdy' pairs with 'nie': nigdy nie mam czasu.
Finding your way and asking directions
The toilet is to the left.
For turning use 'w lewo': skręcić w lewo.
The shop is on the right.
The pharmacy is next to the bank.
The bakery is around the corner.
How do I get to the station?
How do I get to...? (on foot)
How do I get to the market square?
I have a map on my phone.
There's a café on the corner.
Czy jest tu w pobliżu bankomat?
Family members and the people in your life
My dad works at a bank.
Everyday word; formal: 'ojciec'. Masculine despite the -a ending.
Moja siostra ma na imię Ewa.
Mój mąż ma na imię Marek.
My grandpa is eighty years old.
This is my close friend Marek.
A close friend; a casual one is 'znajomy'.
To jest mój znajomy z pracy.
This is an acquaintance of mine from work.
Mój kolega z pracy jest z Ukrainy.
My mate from work is from Ukraine.
From work, school, or the neighbourhood.
To jest mój brat, a to moja siostra.
This is my brother, and this is my sister.
There are a lot of people in the park.
Plural only - the singular is 'człowiek'. 'ludzie' is the subject form, but after 'dużo', 'mało', 'kilku', 'wielu' or a negation it becomes 'ludzi': dużo ludzi, nie ma ludzi.
That gentleman is waiting for the bus.
Also how you politely address a man.
This is my close friend Kasia.
To jest moja znajoma z pracy.
This is an acquaintance of mine from work.
Moja koleżanka z pracy jest z Ukrainy.
My colleague from work is from Ukraine.
That lady is waiting for the bus.
Also how you politely address a woman.
Greetings and the phrases you need in week one
Formal - use any time of day until evening.
Dobry wieczór, stolik dla dwóch osób.
Good evening, a table for two.
Swap in for dzień dobry once it gets dark.
See you, I have to go now.
Please / Here you go / You're welcome
Here you go, this is for you.
Excuse me, where is the exit?
One of the two you'll say most often.
I don't know where it is.
Przepraszam, czy mówi pan po angielsku?
Excuse me, do you speak English?
To a man. To a woman say 'pani' instead of 'pan'.
Informal. In Poland this is a real question, not a passing hello - ask it when you actually want to know, and expect a real answer. A common reply: 'dobrze' - good.
Hey, how's it going with you?
Casual and friendly. Reply lightly: 'wszystko dobrze' or 'po staremu' (same as always).
Breezy, among friends - lighter than 'jak się masz?'. Often answered with a shrug: 'nic nowego' (nothing new).
Also asked as a question to check on someone.
A coffee and a water, please.
Softer than 'chcę'. 'Poproszę kawę' - a coffee, please.
Excuse me, how much is it?
Excuse me, where is the toilet?
The natural reply when someone thanks you.
Here you are, enjoy your meal!
Said before eating - by staff, hosts, or anyone at the table.
A toast when drinking - and also what you say when someone sneezes.
For an exam, a trip, anything ahead.
Warmer than 'do widzenia'; you expect to meet again.
The other one you'll say most often.
The twenty survival verbs you need first
Irregular: jestem, jesteś, jest, jesteśmy, jesteście, są.
I have two cats and a dog.
mam, masz, ma. 'Mam pytanie' = I have a question.
chcę, chcesz, chce. Softer: 'chciałbym' = I would like.
mogę, możesz, może. 'Czy mogę...?' = may I...?
I am going to the shop.
idę, idziesz, idzie. For walking somewhere right now.
I am going to the centre by tram.
jadę, jedziesz, jedzie. For any transport.
What are you doing at the weekend?
robię, robisz, robi. 'Co robisz?' = what are you doing?
mówię, mówisz, mówi. 'Mówię po polsku' = I speak Polish.
I understand, but please speak more slowly.
I don't know where it is.
wiem, wiesz, wie. For facts; for people and places use 'znać'.
znam, znasz, zna. 'Znam Warszawę' = I know Warsaw.
What do you eat for breakfast?
jem, jesz, je. Irregular but essential.
I drink a lot of water.
I buy a ticket in the app.
kupuję, kupujesz. Perfective 'kupić' for a single purchase.
I have lived in Warsaw for a year.
mieszkam, mieszkasz. 'Gdzie mieszkasz?' = where do you live?
I work in an office in the centre.
lubię, lubisz. Takes accusative: lubię kawę.
kocham, kochasz. 'Kocham cię' = I love you.
I am looking for a good café.
szukam, szukasz. Takes genitive: szukam pracy.
I am waiting for the bus.
pomagam, pomagasz. Takes dative: pomagam mamie.
Basic food words and saying what you like
I buy fresh bread at the bakery.
Masculine noun. 'kromka chleba' = a slice of bread.
Na śniadanie jem bułkę z masłem.
For breakfast I eat a roll with butter.
Feminine noun. A breakfast staple in Poland.
'ser żółty' = hard cheese, 'biały ser' = curd cheese.
For breakfast I eat two eggs.
Na obiad jest kurczak z ryżem.
For lunch there is chicken with rice.
On Friday I often eat fish.
I buy vegetables at the market.
I eat a lot of fruit in summer.
Every day I eat one apple.
Neuter noun. Poland is famous for its apples.
I add a tomato to my sandwich.
Na obiad są ziemniaki i kotlet.
For lunch there are potatoes and a cutlet.
Plural of 'ziemniak'. A staple of Polish dinners.
Feminine noun. Poles often start lunch with soup.
I usually eat lunch at two p.m.
The main meal of the day, usually early afternoon.
'To jest bardzo smaczne!' = this is very tasty!
Polish uses this phrase for thirst.
Hobbies and what you like doing in your free time
In my free time I read books.
Masculine phrase. 'W wolnym czasie' = in my free time.
Neuter, does not change form. Plural also 'hobby'.
czytam, czytasz. 'lubię czytać' = I like reading.
In the evening I watch series.
oglądam, oglądasz. For TV, films, matches.
Słucham muzyki w drodze do pracy.
I listen to music on the way to work.
Gram w piłkę w każdą sobotę.
gram, grasz. 'grać w' + sport/game, 'grać na' + instrument.
I'm learning to play the guitar.
'grać na' + instrument in the locative: na gitarze, na pianinie.
I like singing in the shower.
W weekend lubię gotować dla znajomych.
At the weekend I like cooking for friends.
maluję, malujesz. 'rysować' = to draw with a pencil.
In summer I often swim in the lake.
Biegam w parku trzy razy w tygodniu.
I run in the park three times a week.
At the weekend we ride bikes.
Wieczorami gram w gry na komputerze.
In the evenings I play games on the computer.
Video or board games. 'gra planszowa' = board game.
W piątki spotykam się ze znajomymi.
On Fridays I meet up with friends.
I like taking photos when travelling.
Masculine noun. 'uprawiać sport' = to do sport.
Shall we go to a film today?
Masculine noun. 'iść na film' = to go to a film.
I'm reading an interesting book right now.
Co lubisz robić w wolnym czasie?
What do you like doing in your free time?
The key question for small talk about hobbies.
Fruit and vegetables, and buying them at the market
Plural noun. Singular 'owoc' is rare in speech.
Neuter noun. Poland grows a lot of apples.
For breakfast I eat a banana.
In summer I buy strawberries at the market.
I bought green grapes. A woman: kupiłam.
I'm squeezing juice from an orange.
Feminine noun. The fruit; the colour is 'pomarańczowy'.
Feminine noun. 'herbata z cytryną' = tea with lemon.
In autumn I eat a lot of plums.
Feminine noun. 'śliwka' also means a black eye.
W upał nie ma nic lepszego niż arbuz.
In the heat there's nothing better than watermelon.
I add tomatoes to the salad.
Masculine noun. 'ogórek kiszony' = a Polish sour pickle.
I add garlic to almost everything.
Masculine noun. A remedy Poles swear by for colds.
Feminine noun. Both the vegetable and the spice.
Feminine noun. 'sałatka' (with -ka) is a made salad.
Poproszę kilo jabłek i dwie cytryny.
A kilo of apples and two lemons, please.
The core market phrase. The fruit follows in the genitive.
Half a kilo of tomatoes, please.
Months, seasons, and saying when something happens
In January it is very cold.
In April everything is in bloom.
In May the weather is beautiful.
'w maju' = in May. The long weekend 'majówka' starts the month.
In July I have time off.
In August I am going to the seaside.
We wrześniu dzieci wracają do szkoły.
In September children go back to school.
W październiku zaczynają się zajęcia na uczelni.
W listopadzie jest szaro i zimno.
In November it is grey and cold.
'w listopadzie' = in November. From 'liść' (leaf) - leaves falling.
In December there are the holidays.
I have lived here for three months.
'w tym miesiącu' = this month; 'za miesiąc' = in a month.
I have been learning Polish for a year.
'w tym roku' = this year. Plural: lata.
In spring the days get longer and longer.
In summer I go to the lake.
'latem' = in summer. Also the plural of 'rok' (lata = years).
In winter it gets dark early.
Getting up, showering, getting dressed, and having breakfast
Mój budzik dzwoni o siódmej rano.
My alarm clock rings at seven in the morning.
I wake up early in the morning.
Budzę się o szóstej, ale wstaję o wpół do siódmej.
I wake up at six, but I get up at half past six.
First, I go to the bathroom.
In the morning, I usually take a quick shower.
Verb. 'Biorę prysznic' = I take a shower.
I brush my teeth after breakfast.
Literally 'to wash teeth'. 'Myję zęby' = I brush my teeth.
Biorę prysznic i szybko się ubieram.
I take a shower and get dressed quickly.
Neuter noun. Often used in singular.
What do you eat for breakfast?
I am making breakfast for my family.
I eat breakfast at home every day.
I am always very hungry in the morning.
Najpierw piję kawę, a potem jem.
First I drink coffee, and then I eat.
Jem śniadanie, a potem ubieram się.
I eat breakfast, and then I get dressed.
Used to describe what happens next.
Nie mam czasu na śniadanie, spieszę się do pracy.
I don't have time for breakfast, I am in a hurry to work.
Verb. 'Spieszę się' = I am in a hurry (a state). The perfective 'pospieszyć się' means to hurry up on one particular occasion: 'Pospiesz się!' = Hurry up!
Wychodzę z domu o ósmej piętnaście.
I leave the house at eight fifteen.
Numbers, money and paying for things
The tram arrives in ten minutes.
To kosztuje dwa złote pięćdziesiąt groszy.
How much do I pay for everything?
Feminine noun. 'Reszty nie trzeba' uses the genitive of negation.
Everyday weather talk and small-talk openers
In July it is very hot.
At the seaside the wind is always blowing.
Today it is cloudy and grey.
In the morning there was thick fog.
'pięć stopni' = five degrees; 'minus pięć' below zero.
I'm checking the weather forecast for tomorrow.
Check it before a trip: 'sprawdzić prognozę'.
Masculine noun. A woman says: zapomniałam.
Ale brzydka pogoda, cały dzień pada.
What awful weather, it's been raining all day.
The other half of Polish small talk.
Apparently it's going to rain tomorrow.
Renting a flat and dealing with problems
I rent a flat in the centre.

In everyday use it can simply mean the rent. Flat listings often split 'czynsz najmu' (what you pay the landlord) from 'czynsz administracyjny' (the monthly building fee), with utilities on top again.
I have to sign the contract.
There's no electricity in the kitchen.
Is internet included in the price?
The kitchen is small but comfortable.
The bathroom is on the left.
I'm looking for a two-room flat.
'pokój dzienny' = living room; 'kawalerka' = a studio flat.
In the evening we watch a film in the living room.
Where you relax and host guests. Also 'pokój dzienny'.
Leave your shoes in the hallway.
The area just inside the front door where you leave shoes and coats.
In summer I eat breakfast on the balcony.
'z balkonem' = with a balcony - a selling point in listings.
We bought new furniture for the living room.
The bed in the bedroom is comfortable.
Neuter noun. 'iść do łóżka' = go to bed.
There are four chairs at the table.
Plural 'krzesła'. A soft armchair is a 'fotel'.
The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
Hang your coat in the wardrobe.
The milk is in the fridge.
Turn on the stove, I'll cook pasta.
The washing machine is in the bathroom.
A key question when renting: 'Czy jest pralka?'.
I'll put the plates in the dishwasher.
Not in every flat - worth asking about.
I bought a new lamp for the living room.
'żarówka' = light bulb; 'żarówka się przepaliła' = the bulb burnt out.
czas. + biernik · wyglądać na zmęczonego = to look tired.
You look a lot like your brother.
+ dopełniacz · podobny do ojca = like one's father.
Ona ma na sobie czerwoną sukienkę.
+ biernik · the everyday way to say 'wearing'.
In winter I wear a warm hat.
czas. niedok. · for what you wear regularly, not right now.
Put a jacket on, it's cold.
dok. / niedok. · założyć kurtkę = put a jacket on.
I'd like to try on these shoes.
dok. · in a shop: Czy mogę przymierzyć...?
Ten kolor pasuje do twoich oczu.
+ dopełniacz · ten szalik pasuje do płaszcza.
Te spodnie leżą na tobie świetnie.
o ubraniu · ta sukienka leży idealnie = it fits perfectly.
I bought a new dress for the wedding.
rzecz. ż. · letnia sukienka = a summer dress.
I wear a white shirt to work.
rzecz. ż. · koszula w kratkę = a checked shirt.
In winter I don't go out without a jacket.
rzecz. ż. · kurtka przeciwdeszczowa = a rain jacket.
I need new shoes for winter.
rzecz., l. mnoga · para butów = a pair of shoes.
Put a hat on or you'll freeze.
przym. · a polite word for thin (≠ gruby).
przym. · łysy jak kolano = completely bald (idiom).
He grew a beard for the winter.
rzecz. ż. · also means 'chin'. zapuścić brodę = grow a beard.
przym. · ≠ niemodny. modne kolory = trendy colours.
I prefer comfortable shoes to fashionable ones.
przym. · o ubraniach i butach. ≠ niewygodny.
wzory: w kropki (polka dots), w paski (striped), gładki (plain).
What size do you wear, sir?
rzecz. m. · Jaki rozmiar? = What size?
Do twarzy ci w tym kolorze!
idiom · lit. 'it's to your face'. A classic compliment.
Na rozmowę o pracę ubrałem się elegancko.
I dressed smartly for the job interview.
Z jakiego materiału jest ta bluzka?
Masculine noun. 'Z jakiego materiału?' = what's it made of?
This jumper is made of wool.
Feminine noun. 'wełniany sweter' = a wool jumper.
I bought a leather jacket. A woman: kupiłam.
Feminine noun. Both leather and skin.
Feminine noun. Where you try clothes on.
Personality traits - for work and social life
≠ leniwy. A great trait for a CV. Feminine form: pracowita.
≈ precyzyjny. Careful and thorough. Feminine form: dokładna.
Musisz być wytrwały, żeby nauczyć się polskiego.
You have to be persistent to learn Polish.
≈ konsekwentny. Keeps going to the end. Feminine form: wytrwała.
Czasem jestem roztrzepany i gubię klucze.
Sometimes I'm scatterbrained and lose my keys.
Wants to achieve a lot. Feminine form: ambitna.
Expects a lot - of self and others. Feminine form: wymagająca.
Says what they really think. Feminine form: szczera.
Talks a lot (mildly negative). Feminine form: gadatliwa.
≈ naturalny. Says things straight. Feminine form: bezpośrednia.
≠ zamknięty w sobie. Feminine form: otwarta.
Jako dziecko był zamknięty w sobie.
As a child he was withdrawn.
≠ otwarty. Keeps to themselves. Feminine form: zamknięta w sobie.
Jest bardzo towarzyska i ma dużo przyjaciół.
She's very sociable and has lots of friends.
Enjoys company and people. Feminine form: towarzyska.
≈ konfliktowy. Picks arguments. Feminine form: kłótliwa.
Looks after and cares for others. Feminine form: opiekuńcza.
Nasz nowy sąsiad jest bardzo miły.
Our new neighbour is very nice.
One of the most-used compliments in Polish. Feminine form: miła.
≠ spokojny. A personality trait. For feeling nervous right now say 'zdenerwowany / zdenerwowana'.
≠ niecierpliwy. Can wait calmly. Feminine form: cierpliwa.
≈ zimny (of a person). Distant. Feminine form: chłodna.
You're as stubborn as a mule!
Never changes their mind. Idiom: uparty jak osioł. Feminine form: uparta.
Afraid of nothing. Feminine form: odważna.
Na rozmowie o pracę bądź pewny siebie.
At a job interview, be self-confident.
≠ nieśmiały. Self-assured. Feminine form: pewna siebie.
≈ wolny. Doesn't rely on others. Feminine form: niezależna.
≈ despotyczny. Likes to be in control. Feminine form: dominująca.
≈ delikatny. Feels things deeply. Feminine form: wrażliwa.
≠ rozrzutny. Saves money - the positive word. Feminine form: oszczędna.
Don't be stingy, buy a coffee!
Hates spending - the negative twin of oszczędny. Feminine form: skąpa.
Jest rozrzutny i wydaje za dużo.
He's wasteful and spends too much.
≠ oszczędny. Spends too freely. Feminine form: rozrzutna.
I usually get up at seven in the morning.
I drink two coffees every day.
Zazwyczaj wracam do domu po szesnastej.
I usually return home after 4 PM.
On Saturday I clean the whole flat.
I have to wash clothes today.
In the evening I can finally rest.
I go to sleep around midnight.
Reflexive verb. 'Kładę się' = I lie down.
W dni robocze jestem bardzo zajęty.
On weekdays I am very busy.
The past tense: what you did, dates, and memories
Yesterday I was at the cinema.
czas przeszły od 'być' · m: byłem, ż: byłam. The most important past form.
czas przeszły od 'mieć' · miałem czas = I had time.
Robiłem zadanie dwie godziny i w końcu je zrobiłem.
I was doing the task for two hours and finally finished it.
niedok. (proces) vs dok. (wynik) · the core aspect pair.
In the morning I went to the shop.
dok. od 'pójść' · m: poszedłem (careful: 'poszłem' is a common mistake - avoid it), ż: poszłam.
Już ci powiedziałem, że nie mogę.
I already told you I can't.
niedok. vs dok. · different roots, same meaning pair.
I wanted to ask you something.
czas. modalny · chciałem zapytać = I wanted to ask.
I had to get up early.
okolicznik czasu · przedwczoraj = the day before yesterday.
+ miejscownik · also: w zeszłym roku / miesiącu.
Kiedy byłem dzieckiem, mieszkaliśmy na wsi.
When I was a child, we lived in the countryside.
'dziecko' w narzędniku · a set opener for memories.
czas. zwrotny · urodziłem się w 1990 roku.
Przeprowadziłem się tu dwa lata temu.
I moved here two years ago.
'temu' = ago · tydzień temu, miesiąc temu, dawno temu.
On the first of May we have a day off.
daty: liczebnik porządkowy + miesiąc w dopełniaczu.
Urodził się w tysiąc dziewięćset osiemdziesiątym piątym roku.
rok w miejscowniku · only the last part declines: ...osiemdziesiątym piątym.
w tysiąc dziewięćset osiemdziesiątym piątym roku
Back then I didn't know Polish yet.
okolicznik · pairs naturally with past-tense stories.
≠ na końcu (at the end). Good story connector.
Zjedłem śniadanie, a potem poszedłem do pracy.
I ate breakfast and then went to work.
≈ później · sequencing past events: najpierw... potem...
okolicznik · adds drama to a past narrative.
W końcu udało mi się znaleźć mieszkanie.
I finally managed to find a flat.
konstrukcja nieosobowa + celownik · udało mi się + bezokolicznik.
Pamiętam, jak pierwszy raz przyjechałem do Polski.
I remember when I first came to Poland.
Sorry, I forgot about the meeting.
dok. · zapomnieć o czymś = to forget about something.
Asking for directions and finding your way in a city
How do I get to...? (by transport)
Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
How do I get to...? (on foot)
How do I walk to the museum from here?
+ dopełniacz · dojść = reach on foot, dojechać = by vehicle.
the simplest opener · Gdzie jest najbliższy bankomat?
Go straight ahead to the traffic lights.
+ dopełniacz · wzdłuż ulicy = along the street.
Proszę minąć park i skręcić w lewo.
Go past the park and turn left.
dok. + biernik · minąć kościół = pass the church.
The shop is next to the pharmacy.
+ dopełniacz · obok poczty = next to the post office.

nie goes directly before the verb
It stays glued to the verb even in questions: Czy ty nie widzisz?
Compare English's don't / doesn't / didn't / won't - Polish has one word for all of it.
Nie can also negate a single word instead of the verb, and then it stands in front of that word: Nie dziś, tylko jutro.
One position to learn - and no don't / doesn't / didn't to memorise.

Nigdy nie palę - I never smoke. The nie is not optional.
They pile up freely: Nigdy nikomu nic nie mówię - I never tell anyone anything. Four negatives, one meaning.

This only touches direct objects. Other cases stay put: Nie ufam mu (still Dative).

Gender and number come from the noun
którzy is the same masculine-personal club as oni and wszyscy - people-with-a-man get their own form, everything else takes które.
Look left at the noun being described - który copies its gender and number.

The case comes from the clause
Subject of the clause → Nominative: Kobieta, która tu pracuje...
Object of the clause → Accusative: Kobieta, którą poznałem... (I met her → object).
Receiving something → Dative: Dziewczyna, której dałem kwiaty...
This is why the same noun can be followed by different forms - the clause decides.
Gender from the left, case from the right: whatever job który does inside its own clause sets the case.

English says 'the flat I live in'. Polish never leaves the preposition at the end: mieszkanie, w którym mieszkam.

Never both at once: bardziej starszy is the classic learner error.
Polish has a short road and a long road - the adjective decides which one you take.
Notice -ki / -oki drop before the ending: wysoki → wyż-szy, not wysokiszy. The comparative still declines like a normal adjective: starsza siostra, starsze miasto.

The five irregulars you can't skip
These five carry half of daily conversation. If you memorise nothing else from this lesson, memorise lepszy / gorszy / większy / mniejszy.
The most common adjectives are also the most irregular - exactly like English good → better.
This is the best café in Warsaw.
starszy → najstarszy (the oldest), lepszy → najlepszy (the best), gorszy → najgorszy (the worst).
With bardziej the naj- lands on bardziej: najbardziej interesujący.
Superlatives decline too: najlepsza kawa w mieście, najstarsze miasto w Polsce.
Take the comparative you already built and glue naj- on the front. Done.
niż + Nominative - simply continue the sentence: On jest wyższy niż ja.
od + Genitive - the noun changes case: On jest wyższy od brata.
With 'me' the od-version has a special form: wyższy ode mnie.
Both are equally natural - Poles switch between them freely.
Both mean 'than'. They just demand different grammar afterwards - pick whichever you can build fastest.
Superlative works the same way: naj + comparative = najlepiej, najszybciej, najczęściej.
